purpose: Canonical data-to-UI contract for rendering structured lesson practice questions. Used by content authors, UI implementers, QA and future maintainers. This contract describes required UI behavior; it does not mean the components are implemented.

locale_contract.locale_source: One global application language selection, either en or hi.
locale_contract.live_switch: Changing language updates all visible question text and shared controls immediately without resetting the learner response or current question.
localization_required: rubric, sample answer, accepted answer display and status messages
locale_contract.missing_translation_policy: FAIL_VALIDATION_AND_BLOCK_APPROVAL; never silently fall back to the other language.
locale_contract.parity_rule: Language changes presentation only. Question ID, option IDs, expected answers, scoring logic, rubric points and learning objective references remain identical.

practice_session_component.name: PracticeSession
practice_session_component.responsibility: Own the active question index, response map keyed by stable question ID, submission/result status, score and progress. Preserve them when the locale changes.

question_renderer_component.name: PracticeQuestionRenderer
question_renderer_component.responsibility: Dispatch a validated question by its type to exactly one registered question component.
prohibited_behavior: Do not evaluate generated HTML or scripts from lesson JSON.
Do not infer the question type from prose or translate stable IDs.
Do not show a question that references a missing, unapproved or non-student-renderable visual.
Do not use a different grading rule for English and Hindi.

common_accessibility: All controls have localized accessible names, focus indicators and logical keyboard order.
Every interaction is usable with touch and keyboard; drag-only interactions are prohibited.
After submission, announce result and feedback accessibly without moving focus unexpectedly.
Use text and/or icons as well as color; do not use green/red color alone to signal correctness.
Preserve selected/typed responses when locale changes or a question is revisited.
shared_architecture.response_storage: Store answers using locale-neutral IDs/booleans/text and stable matching pairs. Never store a translated option label as the answer key.
shared_architecture.scoring_storage: Store score values and status independently from localized score/feedback text.

question_types.layout: Question prompt followed by a single-select vertical option group; show selection before submission and correctness/feedback after submission.
question_types.input_control: Accessible radio group; exactly one option may be selected.
required_fields: options[] with stable id and text_by_locale.en/hi
validation: At least two unique options.
Exactly one correct_answer_ids entry.
Every option has both locale labels.
Correct ID exists in options.

question_types.layout: Question prompt followed by a vertical checkbox group; multiple answers can be selected.
question_types.input_control: Checkbox group; selected state is an unordered set of option IDs.
required_fields: options[] with stable IDs and bilingual labels
correct_answer_ids[] containing one or more IDs

grading.score: 1 only when selected IDs exactly equal the correct ID set, otherwise 0
grading.note: A future partial-credit change must be versioned and explicitly authored, never guessed by the renderer.

validation: At least two unique options.
At least one valid correct ID.
All correct IDs exist in options.
Every option is bilingual.

question_types.layout: Statement/prompt followed by two equally prominent choices.
question_types.input_control: Radio group or two accessible choice buttons; never use colour as the sole indicator.
validation: correct_answer must be a boolean.
Both locale prompts and feedback are non-empty.

question_types.layout: Two clearly named columns. Each left item pairs with one right item. On narrow screens, render a stacked row per left item with an associated selection control.
question_types.input_control: Accessible select/list choice for each left item; drag and drop may be an enhancement but can never be the only interaction.
required_fields: left_items[] with stable IDs and bilingual labels
right_items[] with stable IDs and bilingual labels

grading.default_score: equal points per left item; score each pair independently
grading.max_score: number of left items unless question-level grading overrides it

validation: Each item ID is unique within its column.
Every correct pair references a valid ID from each column.
Every left item has exactly one correct pair unless an explicit different rule is declared.
Column labels and all item labels are bilingual.

question_types.layout: Sentence/prompt with an inline or clearly adjacent text input; allow submit using a visible button and optionally Enter where appropriate.
question_types.input_control: Single-line text input with localized accessible label and placeholder.

prohibited_normalization: Do not silently translate an answer into the other language.
Do not remove meaningful diacritics/matra or rewrite a student's answer semantically.

validation: Each locale has at least one accepted answer.
Accepted answers are in the corresponding language/script.
Normalization is documented and applied consistently.

question_types.layout: Approved, locale-appropriate image/diagram above the question and response controls; zoom/open control when appropriate; caption and alt text available.
question_types.input_control: Visual panel plus an explicitly declared answer control. For the current item, use a single-select option group matching MultipleChoiceQuestion.
required_fields: alt_by_locale.en/hi or referenced approved asset alt text
options[] and correct_answer_ids for choice-based observation, or a separately specified supported response subtype
question_types.visual_gate: The visual must exist, be approved, student-renderable, rights-cleared where required, relevant to this exact topic, and localized or language-independent. Editor-only full-page source previews cannot satisfy this requirement.
validation: Missing/review-only/unapproved asset blocks learner rendering and publication.
Alt text exists in both languages.
Any visible text embedded in the image is appropriate for the active locale.
The underlying answer control is named explicitly.

question_types.layout: Prompt followed by an accessible multiline text area, character/length guidance if configured, and submit control. After submission show pending-review or rubric feedback as configured.
question_types.input_control: Multiline text area; preserve text when changing language. Do not compare the response to a single exact sample sentence.
required_fields: grading with explicit max_score and bilingual rubric

grading.note: Do not invent automated AI grading behavior. When no validated grader exists, store the response and show a localized pending-review state.

validation: max_score is positive.
Rubric exists in both locales and sums to max_score or defines a valid level scheme.
Key points/sample answer exist in both locales.
No hardcoded single-string exact-match grading.

question_types.layout: A distinct scenario/context card followed by a separate question prompt and an explicitly declared response control. The scenario and question must both switch with the global locale.
question_types.input_control: Use the question's declared response subtype. Current contract version supports choice-based scenarios through a radio group.
required_fields: response subtype fields such as options/correct_answer_ids

response_shape.selected_option_id: string or null for choice-based scenario

validation: Scenario context and prompt are separate fields.
Both are present in both locales.
The subtype and grading rule are explicit.
Scenario remains within the lesson's chapter scope.

known_blockers: The image_observation question currently references a V3 English full-page preview that is editor-only and not student-renderable; replace or approve a suitable bilingual/language-independent visual before rendering/publishing that question.
The Hindi chapter-1 page mapping and paragraph-level source reconciliation remain pending.
The topic has draft question content in both languages but requires semantic translation, answer-key and scope review.

implementation_acceptance: One shared dispatcher renders all supported types by stable question.type and fails closed on unknown types.
Each registered type has a deterministic response schema and grading path with no language-specific differences.
The exact same current lesson is renderable in English and Hindi after assets are resolved, with no mixed-language strings.
A live locale switch preserves every response and all practice-session progress.
Each type passes empty, valid, invalid, submitted-correct, submitted-incorrect and revisit states where relevant.
Keyboard/touch accessibility and narrow-screen layouts pass for all eight components.
Unapproved/missing images, missing translations, missing answers and invalid scoring rules block the affected question from student rendering and publication without crashing unrelated questions.
Existing practice/test functionality remains unaffected; registry adoption is additive.
